# monkeys

> Environment variables kept in your operating system's keyring, handed to one command at a time. No command prints a stored value, and `monkeys run` redacts a value the command prints back. macOS and Linux, MIT.

monkeys is a command line tool. A coding agent spends a secret with `monkeys run NAME <command>`: the value goes from the keyring into that one process's environment and never through the conversation. A project lists the names it needs in a `.monkeys` file under a profile, and `pack` and `unpack` move a profile between machines as one encrypted file.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/eastriverlee/monkeys#readme): install, every command, projects and profiles, sharing a profile, what gets redacted
- [Skill for coding agents](https://github.com/eastriverlee/monkeys/blob/main/skills/monkeys/SKILL.md): the rules an agent follows when it uses monkeys
- [Full text](https://monk3ys.dev/llms-full.txt): the README and the skill in one file

## Install

- [Install script](https://monk3ys.dev/install): `curl -fsSL https://monk3ys.dev/install | sh`
- [Homebrew tap](https://github.com/eastriverlee/homebrew-tap): `brew install eastriverlee/tap/monkeys`
- [Releases](https://github.com/eastriverlee/monkeys/releases): prebuilt binaries for macOS and Linux

## Optional

- [Source](https://github.com/eastriverlee/monkeys): Swift, no runtime dependencies
